title: Level 2: Arrays & Loops
description: Master looping techniques, array methods like map/filter/reduce, and real-world array challenges.

notes.title: What is an Array?
notes.content: An array is a special variable that can hold multiple values in a single reference. Values are stored by index, starting at 0.
notes.deepDive: Arrays in JS are objects with numeric keys and have methods like `push`, `pop`, `map`, etc.

notes.title: Looping with for
notes.content: The `for` loop runs a block of code a specific number of times—ideal for iterating arrays.
notes.deepDive: Using `let` in the loop header creates a new `i` for each iteration due to block scope.

notes.title: Looping with while
notes.content: `while` loops run as long as a condition is true—useful when number of iterations isn’t known ahead.
notes.deepDive: `do...while` runs once before checking the condition, ensuring at least one iteration.

notes.title: Array length behavior
notes.content: The `.length` property returns the number of items in an array. Assigning a higher index increases length.
notes.deepDive: Setting `.length` shorter truncates items; longer adds empty slots.

notes.title: push & pop methods
notes.content: `push` adds to end, `pop` removes from end. They modify the array.
notes.deepDive: These are O(1) operations — ideal for stack-like behavior.

notes.title: shift & unshift methods
notes.content: `shift` removes first element, `unshift` adds one or more to beginning. They mutate and are slower.
notes.deepDive: These operations are O(n), so avoid on large arrays frequently.

notes.title: Map, Filter, Reduce
notes.content: `map` returns a new array by transforming elements; `filter` creates a subset; `reduce` aggregates values.
notes.deepDive: `reduce` can be used to implement map, filter, and more—it's very flexible.

notes.title: for...of vs for...in
notes.content: `for...of` iterates values, `for...in` iterates keys (properties). Use correctly.
notes.deepDive: `for...in` also includes keys added via prototype chain—use with care.

notes.title: Nested loops
notes.content: Use loops inside loops to iterate nested structures like grids or multidimensional arrays.
notes.deepDive: Nested loops can significantly affect performance—O(n²) for 2D arrays.

notes.title: break and continue
notes.content: `break` exits loop; `continue` skips to the next iteration.
notes.codeSnippet: for(let x of arr){ if(x===3) break; if(x%2) continue; console.log(x); }
notes.deepDive: Using these controls can complicate logic readability—use with caution.

notes.title: Debugging loops
notes.content: Use `console.log`, breakpoints, and tools to inspect loop behavior.
notes.deepDive: DevTools can step through iterations, allowing breakpoints inside loops.

notes.title: Type Conversion in Loops
notes.content: Beware implicit type conversion when accumulating values in loops.
notes.codeSnippet:
let total=''; for(let x of [1,2,3]) total+=x;
console.log(typeof total); // string
notes.deepDive: Always convert types explicitly if expecting numbers or strings.

mcqs.question: [1,2,3].map(x => x * 2)
mcqs.explanation: `map()` creates a new array with the result of calling a function on every element.

mcqs.question: [1,2,3].filter(x => x > 1)
mcqs.explanation: `filter()` returns elements that satisfy the condition.

mcqs.question: [1,2,3].reduce((a,b)=>a+b, 0)
mcqs.explanation: `reduce()` aggregates values; here it sums the array.

mcqs.question: [].map(() => 1)
mcqs.explanation: Mapping an empty array returns an empty array.

mcqs.question: [].filter(() => true)
mcqs.explanation: Filtering an empty array returns empty.

mcqs.question: Array.concat(a,b) vs [...a, ...b]
mcqs.explanation: Both concatenate and return a new array.

mcqs.question: What does splice return?
mcqs.explanation: `splice()` returns an array of removed elements.
Arrays are coerced to strings during concatenation.

mcqs.question: for...of loops:
mcqs.explanation: `for...of` iterates over iterable values.

mcqs.question: for...in loops:
mcqs.explanation: `for...in` iterates over property keys.

mcqs.question: do...while guarantees:
mcqs.explanation: It executes the loop before condition checking.

mcqs.question: Using let in for loop:
mcqs.explanation: `let` confines i to the loop scope.

mcqs.question: continue does:
mcqs.explanation: It skips current iteration.

mcqs.question: break does:
mcqs.explanation: It exits the loop entirely.

mcqs.question: Array.reverse():
mcqs.explanation: It changes the original array.

mcqs.question: slice(0,2) vs splice(0,2)
mcqs.explanation: `slice()` doesn't modify the original array.

mcqs.question: Spread [...] on array:
mcqs.explanation: It copies array elements shallowly.

mcqs.question: reduce() without initial:
mcqs.explanation: The first item becomes accumulator.

mcqs.question: while(i<0){ }
mcqs.explanation: Condition false, no iteration.

mcqs.question: for(;;){ }
mcqs.explanation: No condition defaults to true.

mcqs.question: filter(() => false)
mcqs.explanation: Empty array results from filtering all out.

mcqs.question: map(() => undefined)
mcqs.explanation: Mapping to undefined yields an array of undefined values.
